steps.prompt: Before the check: which part of this unit feels easiest, and which do you want to look at again?

cards.title: Building sentences: quick review
cards.body: A sentence needs a subject and a predicate. Subjects and predicates can be compound (Maya and Leo built it; Maya built and tested it). A phrase has no subject and verb; a clause does. A dependent clause (because…, when…, which…) can’t stand alone, and it takes a comma after it when it comes first.

cards.title: Fixing sentences: quick review
cards.body: Fragment: join it to a neighbour or add what’s missing. Run-on or comma splice: use a full stop, a semicolon, a comma + and/but/or/so, or make one part a dependent clause. However and then need a semicolon or a full stop before them.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write an opinion paragraph that shows off your sentence building. Quill gives it a score.
